{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "# This workflow will upload a Python Package using Twine when a release is created
# For more information see: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/automating-builds-and-tests/building-and-testing-python#publishing-to-package-registries

# This workflow uses actions that are not certified by GitHub.
# They are provided by a third-party and are governed by
# separate terms of service, privacy policy, and support
# documentation.

name: Upload Python Package

on:
  release:
    types: [published]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  deploy:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    - name: Set up Python
      uses: actions/setup-python@v3
      with:
        python-version: '3.10'
    - name: Cache pip dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.cache/pip
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('pyproject.toml') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-pip-
    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        python -m pip install poetry
    - name: Build package
      run: poetry build
    - name: Publish package
      uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
      with:
        password: ${{ secrets.PYPI_API_TOKEN }}",
  "rationale": "The workflow runs `pip install poetry` on every release, repeatedly fetching dependencies. Evidence pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (cache dependency downloads) supports adding a pip cache keyed on the dependency manifest (pyproject.toml) and runner OS, with restore keys; the measured experiment example showed about 9% elapsed reduction from the same cache step. This preserves all build/publish steps and required checks, adds no privileges, secrets, publishing changes, or new network access beyond pip's existing use.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE", "experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2"]
}
